def-quotient-sheaf-and-representable-quo.title: Quotient sheaves and representable quotients for pre-relations and group actions
def-quotient-sheaf-and-representable-quo.statement: Let $k$ be a field, and let $s,t:R\to U$ be two morphisms of $k$-schemes with common target ([[def-morphism-of-schemes]]); such a pair is a **pre-relation** on $U$. The **naive quotient presheaf** $P_{U/R}$ is the functor on the category of $k$-schemes sending a $k$-scheme $T$ to the quotient of the set $U(T)$ ([[def-fibre-product-schemes-universal-property]]) by the equivalence relation generated by $\{(s(x),t(x)):x\in R(T)\}$; its value at $T=\operatorname{Spec}k$ is the set of $k$-points of $U$ modulo the relation generated by $R(k)$. $P_{U/R}$ is in general only a presheaf ([[def-presheaf-representable-functor-and-representation]]). An **fppf sheaf** on this category is a presheaf $F$ such that for every $k$-scheme $T$ and every fppf covering family $\{T_i\to T\}$ — a finite family of flat morphisms locally of finite presentation whose disjoint union is surjective onto $T$ ([[def-faithfully-flat-morphism-schemes]], [[def-locally-finite-presentation-morphism]]) — the diagram $F(T)\to\prod_iF(T_i)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}F(T_i\times_TT_j)$ is an equalizer. The **fppf quotient sheaf** $U/R$ is the sheafification of $P_{U/R}$ for this topology: a morphism $P_{U/R}\to U/R$ of presheaves with $U/R$ an fppf sheaf, initial among morphisms from $P_{U/R}$ to fppf sheaves. Every representable presheaf is an fppf sheaf ([[lem-nonaffine-fppf-descent-of-scheme-morphisms]]); a $k$-scheme $M$ **represents the quotient sheaf** $U/R$ when there is a natural isomorphism $h_M\cong U/R$ ([[def-presheaf-representable-functor-and-representation]]), and then $M$ is unique up to unique isomorphism. For a group scheme $G$ of finite type over $k$ ([[def-group-scheme-over-a-field]]) acting on $U$ one takes $R=G\times_kU$ with $s$ the second projection and $t$ the action morphism, and writes $U/G$; for $U=G$ and a closed subgroup scheme $H\subseteq G$ ([[def-morphism-and-closed-subgroup-scheme]]) acting by right translation one takes $R=G\times_kH$, $s(g,h)=g$, $t(g,h)=gh$, and writes $G/H$. The quotient sheaf is generally strictly bigger than the naive quotient presheaf; the orbit set is only $P_{U/R}(k)$.
def-quotient-sheaf-and-representable-quo.strategy: Definition record following Stacks Definition 39.20.1 (tag 02VG) and Definition 39.20.2 (tag 03BD), with the fppf topology of Stacks Section 34.7 (tags 021Q, 021R, 021S) and the sheaf condition of Stacks Section 7.7 (tag 00VM). The naive quotient is only a presheaf, so its sheafification must be defined; represented functors are fppf sheaves by the published descent lemma for scheme morphisms. No claim of representability is made in the definition.

def-algebraic-group-action-and-scheme-th.title: Algebraic group actions, orbit maps, orbit subschemes and scheme-theoretic stabilizers
def-algebraic-group-action-and-scheme-th.statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $G$ be a group scheme of finite type over $k$ ([[def-group-scheme-over-a-field]]) and let $X$ be a $k$-scheme ([[def-scheme-over-base]]). An **action** of $G$ on $X$ is a morphism $\alpha:G\times_kX\to X$ ([[def-morphism-of-schemes]]) such that the unit and associativity diagrams commute: $\alpha(e\times\operatorname{id}_X)=\operatorname{id}_X$ and $\alpha(\operatorname{id}_G\times\alpha)=\alpha(m\times\operatorname{id}_X)$, where $m$ is the multiplication of $G$. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ of $k$-schemes on which $G$ acts is **equivariant** if $f\alpha_X=\alpha_Y(\operatorname{id}_G\times f)$. The action is determined by its values on $R$-points, giving an action of the abstract group $G(R)$ on $X(R)$ for every $k$-algebra $R$. For $x\in X(k)$ ([[lem-field-valued-points-of-schemes]]) the **orbit map** is $\varrho_x:G\to X$, $\varrho_x(g)=\alpha(g,x)$; its image, with the reduced subscheme structure, is the **orbit subscheme** $O_x$ ([[def-scheme-theoretic-image]], [[def-locally-closed-immersion]]). The **scheme-theoretic stabilizer** (isotropy group) is the fibre product $G_x:=G\times_{X}\operatorname{Spec}k$ formed with $\varrho_x$ and the $k$-point $x$ ([[def-scheme-theoretic-fibre]], [[def-fibre-product-schemes-universal-property]]): it is a closed subscheme of $G$, and for every $k$-algebra $R$ its $R$-points are $G_x(R)=\{g\in G(R):\alpha(g,x_R)=x_R\}$. The pair $R=G\times_kX\rightrightarrows X$ with $s(g,z)=z$ and $t(g,z)=\alpha(g,z)$ is the **action groupoid** of the action, a pre-relation on $X$ ([[def-quotient-sheaf-and-representable-quotient]]). When $X$ is separated and of finite type over $k$, $k$-points are closed, so $G_x$ is a closed subgroup scheme of $G$ ([[def-morphism-and-closed-subgroup-scheme]]).
def-algebraic-group-action-and-scheme-th.strategy: Definition record following Milne, Algebraic Groups (2022), Chapter 7 Sections 7(c)-(b), printed pp. 139-140 (orbit maps, isotropy groups defined as fibres of the orbit map, orbit subschemes), and Brion, Introduction to actions of algebraic groups, Definition 1.4 and Definition 1.10, printed pp. 3-5. The stabilizer is introduced as the fibre product so that it is a priori a scheme, not merely a subgroup of points; closedness of the fibre uses that a $k$-point of a separated finite-type $k$-scheme is a closed point. The action groupoid is recorded because the quotient sheaf of this page is the quotient of that pre-relation.

lem-action-map-fibres-and-stabilizer-sub.title: Fibres of the orbit map and the scheme-theoretic stabilizer as a closed subgroup scheme
lem-action-map-fibres-and-stabilizer-sub.statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $G$ be a group scheme of finite type over $k$ acting on a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ ([[def-algebraic-group-action-and-scheme-theoretic-stabilizer]]), and let $x\in X(k)$. (a) The scheme-theoretic stabilizer $G_x$ is a closed subscheme of $G$, is a subgroup scheme of $G$ ([[def-morphism-and-closed-subgroup-scheme]]), and for every $k$-algebra $R$ the identification $G_x(R)=\{g\in G(R):\alpha(g,x_R)=x_R\}$ holds ([[lem-closed-subgroup-scheme-valued-point-criterion]]). (b) For $y\in X(k)$ with $y=g_0x$ for some $g_0\in G(k)$ the fibre $\varrho_x^{-1}(y)$ is the left translate $g_0G_x$, and in general the fibre over $y$ is empty unless $y$ lies in the orbit $O_x$; for $g\in G(k)$ one has $G_{gx}=gG_xg^{-1}$. (c) The morphism $\Phi:G\times_kX\to X\times_kX$, $\Phi(g,z)=(\alpha(g,z),z)$ ([[def-fibre-product-schemes-universal-property]]), has scheme-theoretic fibre over the $k$-point $(y,x)$ canonically isomorphic, via the first projection, to the fibre of the orbit map $\varrho_x$ over $y$ ([[def-scheme-theoretic-fibre]]); this fibre is empty when $y\notin O_x$ and is a translate of $G_x$ when nonempty. (d) The kernel-pair morphism $G\times_kG_x\to G\times_{O_x}G$, $(g,h)\mapsto(g,gh)$, is an isomorphism of $k$-schemes; equivalently, for every $k$-algebra $R$ the map $G(R)\times G_x(R)\to\{(g,g')\in G(R)\times G(R): gx_R=g'x_R\}$, $(g,h)\mapsto(g,gh)$, is a bijection.
lem-action-map-fibres-and-stabilizer-sub.strategy: Follow Milne, Chapter 7 Section 7(c), printed pp. 139-140 (the isotropy group is the fibre of the orbit map and is a closed subgroup scheme), and Brion, Proposition 1.11, printed pp. 5-6. (a) The fibre of a morphism over a closed point is a closed subscheme; since $X$ is separated and of finite type over $k$, the section $x:\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ is a closed immersion, so $G_x=G\times_X\operatorname{Spec}k$ is closed in $G$; the functor-of-points description is the universal property of the fibre product. That $G_x$ is a subgroup scheme is the functor-of-points computation $g,h\in G_x(R)\Rightarrow gh^{-1}\in G_x(R)$, using the published valued-point criterion for closed subgroup schemes. (b) Translate by $g_0$: right? left multiplication by $g_0$ is an automorphism of $G$ carrying $\varrho_x^{-1}(x)$ to $\varrho_x^{-1}(g_0x)$, giving the stated identification and the conjugacy formula. (c) Compute on $R$-points: $\Phi(g,z)=(y,x)$ forces $z=x_R$ and $gx_R=y$. (d) On $R$-points, from $gx_R=g'x_R$ we get $g^{-1}g'\in G_x(R)$, so $(g,g')=(g,gh)$ for the unique $h=g^{-1}g'$; conversely $(g,gh)$ has equal images. The identification is natural in $R$, hence an isomorphism by Yoneda; the fibre product is computed on points by the universal property.

lem-fppf-quotient-representability-crite.title: Criterion for a scheme to represent an fppf quotient sheaf
lem-fppf-quotient-representability-crite.statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $s,t:R\to U$ be a pre-relation on $k$-schemes with fppf quotient sheaf $U/R$ ([[def-quotient-sheaf-and-representable-quotient]]), and let $q:U\to M$ be a morphism to a $k$-scheme $M$. Assume: (1) $q\circ s=q\circ t$; (2) $q$ induces a surjection of fppf sheaves $h_U\to h_M$ (for instance, $q$ is faithfully flat and locally of finite presentation); (3) the morphism $(t,s):R\to U\times_MU$ ([[def-fibre-product-schemes-universal-property]]) induces a surjection of fppf sheaves $h_R\to h_{U\times_MU}$ (for instance $(t,s)$ is faithfully flat and locally of finite presentation). Then $M$ represents the quotient sheaf $U/R$.
lem-fppf-quotient-representability-crite.strategy: This is Stacks Lemma 39.20.3 (tag 03C5), transcribed. Condition (1) says that $h_U\to h_M$ factors through $U/R$; condition (2) says the induced map $U/R\to h_M$ is surjective as a map of sheaves; condition (3) says it is injective, because a map of fppf sheaves $U/R\to h_M$ is injective as soon as $h_R\to h_{U\times_MU}$ is surjective (two $M$-points of $U$ that are $R$-related must agree). Representable functors are fppf sheaves by the published scheme-descent lemma, so the sheaf-theoretic argument applies to the representing objects.

lem-projective-space-action-from-linear-.title: A linear representation induces an action on projective space with the same line stabilizers
lem-projective-space-action-from-linear-.statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $G$ be a group scheme of finite type over $k$, let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space, and let $r:G\to\operatorname{GL}_V$ be a rational representation ([[def-rational-representation-and-comodule-of-an-affine-group-scheme]]). Let $P(V)=\mathbb P_k(V\otimes_k\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}k})$ be the projective bundle of the constant finite locally free sheaf $V\otimes_k\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}k}$ in the quotient convention, so that for every $k$-scheme $T$ the set $P(V)(T)$ is naturally the set of isomorphism classes of surjections $V\otimes_k\mathcal O_T\twoheadrightarrow L$ onto an invertible $\mathcal O_T$-module ([[def-projective-bundle-scheme]], [[thm-projective-bundle-represents-line-quotients]]). (a) There is a unique action $\alpha:G\times_kP(V)\to P(V)$ ([[def-algebraic-group-action-and-scheme-theoretic-stabilizer]]) whose effect on $T$-points sends the class of $q:V\otimes_k\mathcal O_T\to L$ and $g\in G(T)$ to the class of $q\circ r(g)^{-1}$. (b) If $L\subseteq V$ is a line with class $[L]\in P(V)(k)$ and $q_L:V\to V/L$ is the quotient map, then for every $k$-algebra $R$ the stabilizer of $[L]$ satisfies $G_{[L]}(R)=\{g\in G(R): r(g)(L_R)=L_R\}$ ([[def-algebraic-group-action-and-scheme-theoretic-stabilizer]], [[lem-action-map-fibres-and-stabilizer-subscheme]]). In particular, if $H\subseteq G$ is a closed subgroup scheme whose $R$-points are exactly those $g$ with $r(g)(L_R)=L_R$, then $G_{[L]}=H$.
lem-projective-space-action-from-linear-.strategy: Milne, Chapter 7 Section 7(d)-(e), printed pp. 141-143: $\mathbb P^n$ represents the functor of rank-one direct summands (here the equivalent invertible-quotient form supplied by the published projective-bundle theorem), so by the Yoneda lemma a natural action on $T$-points defines a morphism $G\times_kP(V)\to P(V)$. For (a): the assignments $g\mapsto r(g)^{-1}$ are natural in $T$ and multiplicative, so they define an action of the group functor $G$ on the functor $P(V)$; the groupoid and identity axioms are checked pointwise and give the commutative diagrams for $\alpha$. For (b): $q\circ r(g)^{-1}$ has the same kernel line as $q$ if and only if $r(g)$ preserves $L_R$; the functor-of-points description of the fibre product computes the stabilizer. No smoothness of $G$ is used, only that $r$ is a morphism of group functors.

lem-orbit-map-faithfully-flat-and-orbit-.title: Smooth orbits are locally closed and their orbit maps are faithfully flat over every field
lem-orbit-map-faithfully-flat-and-orbit-.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field, let $G$ be a smooth algebraic group scheme of finite type over $k$ ([[def-smooth-morphism-schemes]]) acting on a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ ([[def-algebraic-group-action-and-scheme-theoretic-stabilizer]]), and let $x\in X(k)$ ([[lem-action-map-fibres-and-stabilizer-subscheme]]). Then the orbit subscheme $O_x$ is locally closed in $X$ and stable under $G$, and the orbit map $\varrho_x:G\to O_x$ is faithfully flat and locally of finite presentation. In particular $O_x$ is smooth over $k$ and of finite type. The Axiom of Choice is used exactly as in the generic-flatness and constructibility inputs below.
lem-orbit-map-faithfully-flat-and-orbit-.strategy: This is Milne, Proposition 1.65(b)-(c) together with Proposition 7.4(b), printed pp. 27-28 and 139-140. Step 1 (reduce to an algebraically closed base): the underlying-space map $|X_{k^a}|\to|X|$ is a quotient (indeed open) map and flatness descends along the faithfully flat base change $k\to k^a$; hence it suffices to prove the assertions after base change to an algebraic closure, as in Milne 1.65(b) and A.20. Step 2 (local closedness): over $k^a$, the image of the morphism $\varrho_x$ is constructible by the published Chevalley theorem for varieties, so it contains a dense open subset $U$ of its closure; since $G(k^a)$ acts transitively on the orbit and the action is by automorphisms, the translates of $U$ cover the orbit and exhibit it as open in its closure, hence locally closed; this is Milne 1.65(b). Step 3 (faithful flatness): apply generic flatness to the restriction of $\varrho_x$ over an integral chart of the closure; flatness holds over a dense open. Because the morphism is equivariant for the transitive action of $G(k^a)$ and the translates of the flat locus are flat by base change along automorphisms, flatness holds everywhere; surjectivity onto the orbit gives faithful flatness (Milne 1.65(a) with A.70). Step 4 (smoothness): faithful flatness gives an injection $\mathcal O_{O_x}\to(\varrho_x)_*\mathcal O_G$ that remains injective after base change, so $O_x$ is geometrically reduced; its smooth locus is nonempty and stable under the transitive action, hence all of $O_x$ (Milne 7.4(b) with A.55). Stability under $G$ and finite presentation are immediate from the construction.

lem-orbit-map-fibres-and-stabilizer-dime.title: Fibre dimension and orbit dimension add to the dimension of the group
lem-orbit-map-fibres-and-stabilizer-dime.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $G$ be a connected smooth algebraic group scheme of finite type over $k$ (such a $G$ is separated by Milne 1.22 and geometrically reduced, hence a classical variety of finite type over $k$) acting on a classical variety $X$ over $k$ ([[def-dimension-classical-variety]], [[cor-smooth-variety-classical-scheme-conventions-agree]]), and let $x\in X(k)$ be a closed point. Then: (a) every nonempty fibre of the orbit map $\varrho_x:G\to O_x$ is a left translate of the stabilizer $G_x$ ([[lem-action-map-fibres-and-stabilizer-subscheme]]), hence has dimension $\dim G_x$ in the sense of [[def-dimension-classical-variety]]; (b) $\dim G=\dim G_x+\dim O_x$; (c) the orbit closure $\overline{O_x}$ is the union of $O_x$ and of orbits of strictly smaller dimension; consequently every orbit of minimal dimension in $X$ is closed, and $\overline{O_x}$ contains a closed orbit. The Axiom of Choice is inherited from the generic-fibre and constructibility inputs.
lem-orbit-map-fibres-and-stabilizer-dime.strategy: This is Milne, Proposition 5.23 for the dimension identity and the Orbit Lemma 1.66 with Propositions 7.4-7.6 for the closure statements, printed pp. 27-28, 104-105 and 139-140, with Brion, Proposition 1.11, printed pp. 5-6, as the independent treatment. (a) By the orbit-map lemma every nonempty fibre of $\varrho_x$ is a left translate of $G_x$, and left translation by an element of $G(k)$ is an isomorphism of varieties, so all nonempty fibres have the same dimension as $G_x$. (b) The orbit map is dominant onto the irreducible variety $O_x$ with all nonempty fibres of pure dimension $\dim G_x$ (in particular this is the generic fibre dimension), so the published generic-fibre-dimension theorem gives $\dim G-\dim O_x=\dim G_x$. (c) If an orbit $O'$ meets $\overline{O_x}\setminus O_x$, then $\overline{O'}\subseteq\overline{O_x}\setminus O_x$ and this difference is a union of finitely many nonempty locally closed subsets of strictly smaller dimension, so $\dim O'<\dim O_x$; iterating with the finite union of components and using that dimensions are nonnegative integers gives that an orbit of minimal dimension is closed, and that the closure of any orbit contains one. This is Milne 1.66 and 7.6 in the classical-variety setting.

prop-faithfully-flat-orbit-map-represent.title: A faithfully flat orbit map represents the coset quotient sheaf
prop-faithfully-flat-orbit-map-represent.statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $G$ be a group scheme of finite type over $k$ acting on a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ ([[def-algebraic-group-action-and-scheme-theoretic-stabilizer]]), let $x\in X(k)$, and let $H$ be a closed subgroup scheme of $G$ ([[def-morphism-and-closed-subgroup-scheme]]) with $H=G_x$ ([[lem-action-map-fibres-and-stabilizer-subscheme]]). Assume the orbit map $\varrho_x:G\to O_x$ is faithfully flat and locally of finite presentation, where $O_x$ is the orbit subscheme. Then $O_x$ represents the fppf quotient sheaf $G/H$ ([[def-quotient-sheaf-and-representable-quotient]]), the quotient morphism is $\varrho_x$, and the kernel-pair morphism $G\times_kH\to G\times_{O_x}G$, $(g,h)\mapsto(g,gh)$, is an isomorphism.
prop-faithfully-flat-orbit-map-represent.strategy: Apply the representability criterion (Stacks 39.20.3) to the pre-relation $R=G\times_kH\rightrightarrows U=G$ with $s(g,h)=g$, $t(g,h)=gh$, and $q=\varrho_x:U\to O_x$. Condition (1) holds because $H=G_x$ fixes $x$, so $\varrho_x(gh)=(gh)x=gx=\varrho_x(g)$. Condition (2) holds by the faithful flatness and finite presentation of $\varrho_x$. Condition (3) is the kernel-pair isomorphism supplied for the orbit by the fibre computation of the orbit-map lemma, transported along the identification $H=G_x$: on $R$-points, $(g,h)\mapsto(g,gh)$ is a bijection onto the pairs of $G(R)$ with equal image in $O_x(R)$. This is Milne's proof of Proposition 7.11, with the quotient sheaf formulation of Stacks 39.20.

thm-homogeneous-space-for-smooth-affine-.title: Homogeneous spaces of smooth affine groups are separated schemes
thm-homogeneous-space-for-smooth-affine-.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field, let $G$ be a smooth affine group scheme of finite type over $k$ ([[def-smooth-morphism-schemes]]) and let $H\subseteq G$ be a closed subgroup scheme ([[def-morphism-and-closed-subgroup-scheme]]). Then the fppf quotient sheaf $G/H$ ([[def-quotient-sheaf-and-representable-quotient]]) is representable by a separated $k$-scheme of finite type, unique up to unique isomorphism, and the quotient morphism $G\to G/H$ is faithfully flat and locally of finite presentation. Moreover there are a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space $V$, a rational representation $r:G\to\operatorname{GL}_V$ ([[def-rational-representation-and-comodule-of-an-affine-group-scheme]]) and a line $L\subseteq V$ with scheme-theoretic line stabilizer $H$, such that $G/H$ is isomorphic to the orbit $O_{[L]}$ of $[L]$ under the induced action on $P(V)$ ([[lem-projective-space-action-from-linear-representation]]) and the resulting morphism $G/H\to P(V)$ is an immersion ([[def-locally-closed-immersion]]). In particular $G/H$ is separated and finite type over $k$, and no smoothness of $H$ is required. The Axiom of Choice is used through the generic-flatness, constructibility and Chevalley inputs cited in the proof.
thm-homogeneous-space-for-smooth-affine-.strategy: This is Milne, Theorem 7.18, printed p. 143, with Proposition 7.17, printed p. 143. Step 1: Chevalley's theorem, in the published local form [[lem-nonaffine-subgroup-scheme-stabilizer-of-line]], supplies a finite-dimensional representation $V$ of $G$ and a line $L\subseteq V$ whose scheme-theoretic stabilizer is exactly $H$; no smoothness of $H$ or of the representation is used. Step 2: by [[lem-projective-space-action-from-linear-representation]] the representation induces an action of $G$ on $P(V)$ (a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, by the published closed-diagonal lemma for relative projective space) such that the scheme-theoretic stabilizer of the point $[L]$ is $H$. Step 3: take $x=[L]$ and $O_x\subseteq P(V)$ its orbit subscheme. Since $G$ is smooth, [[lem-orbit-map-faithfully-flat-and-orbit-locally-closed]] applies over the given field: $O_x$ is locally closed and smooth, and $\varrho_x:G\to O_x$ is faithfully flat and locally of finite presentation. In particular the hypotheses of Step 4 hold. Step 4: [[prop-faithfully-flat-orbit-map-represents-coset-quotient]] shows that $O_x$ represents the fppf quotient sheaf $G/H$ with quotient morphism $\varrho_x$. Step 5: $O_x$ is a locally closed subscheme of the separated finite-type $k$-scheme $P(V)$, so it is separated and finite type over $k$ by the published stability of separatedness under immersions; uniqueness of the representing object is Yoneda. The AC use is exactly that of the generic-flatness and constructibility inputs in Step 3 and of the Chevalley input in Step 1.

thm-fppf-quotient-for-affine-finite-loca.title: Affine finite locally free equivalence relations have finite locally free scheme quotients
thm-fppf-quotient-for-affine-finite-loca.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field, let $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $R=\operatorname{Spec}B$ be affine finite-type $k$-schemes, and let $s,t:R\to U$ be finite locally free morphisms ([[def-faithfully-flat-morphism-schemes]]) such that $j=(t,s):R\to U\times_kU$ is an equivalence relation. Put $C=\{a\in A: s^\sharp(a)=t^\sharp(a)\}$ ([[def-quotient-sheaf-and-representable-quotient]] for the quotient sheaf $U/R$). Then $C$ is a finite-type $k$-algebra, the morphism $U\to M=\operatorname{Spec}C$ is finite locally free and surjective, the canonical morphism $R\to U\times_MU$ is an isomorphism, and $M$ represents the fppf quotient sheaf $U/R$.
thm-fppf-quotient-for-affine-finite-loca.strategy: This is the affine finite-locally-free case of Stacks Proposition 39.23.9 (tag 03BM), recorded in the form used by this page and discharged by the published theorem [[thm-nonaffine-finite-flat-affine-equivalence-quotient]], which proves exactly this statement for affine finite-type schemes over a field: $C$ is finite type, $U\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ is finite locally free and onto, $R\cong U\times_MU$, and $M$ represents the fppf quotient sheaf. The only reconciliation is the notion of quotient sheaf: the published theorem's phrase 'represents the fppf quotient sheaf $U/R$' is the notion defined in [[def-quotient-sheaf-and-representable-quotient]] (sheafification of the naive quotient presheaf in the fppf topology), so no hypothesis is added and no step of the published proof is repeated. The source remains Stacks 39.23.9; the design's promise for this pair is covered by this recorded interface.

rem-quotient-sheaf-versus-representing-s.title: Orbit sets, fppf quotient sheaves and representing schemes are three different objects
rem-quotient-sheaf-versus-representing-s.statement: Three objects are commonly conflated, and must be kept apart. (1) The **orbit set** $U(k)/R(k)$: the value at $k$ of the naive quotient presheaf of a pre-relation; it is computed from $k$-points alone. (2) The **fppf quotient sheaf** $U/R$ ([[def-quotient-sheaf-and-representable-quotient]]): the sheafification of that presheaf, whose sections over a $k$-scheme $T$ are fppf-local orbit data. Its $k$-points can be strictly larger than the orbit set, and it carries infinitesimal information invisible to it; a concrete instance is recorded on the examples companion page of this pair. (3) A **representing scheme**: a $k$-scheme $M$ with a natural isomorphism $h_M\cong U/R$ ([[lem-fppf-quotient-representability-criterion]]); by Yoneda it is unique up to unique isomorphism when it exists. Representability is an additional property, not a consequence of the definitions: this page establishes it for homogeneous spaces of smooth affine groups ([[thm-homogeneous-space-for-smooth-affine-group]]) and for affine finite locally free equivalence relations ([[thm-fppf-quotient-for-affine-finite-locally-free-equivalence-relation]]). In the homogeneous-space case the quotient is the orbit of the base point and the quotient morphism is faithfully flat ([[prop-faithfully-flat-orbit-map-represents-coset-quotient]]); the general arbitrary-group quotient representability statement is outside the scope of this page and is not claimed here.
rem-quotient-sheaf-versus-representing-s.strategy: Remark separating the three notions, following Stacks Definition 39.20.1 and Section 66.14 and Milne, Chapter 5 Section 5(c) and Chapter 7 Section 7(e). The distinction between the orbit set and the quotient sheaf is made precise by the orbit-set counterexample on the examples companion page; the distinction between a quotient sheaf and a representing scheme is exactly the gap between Definition 39.20.1 and the representability statements proved here. The remark deliberately claims representability only in the two cases proved, matching the design's source gate on general arbitrary-group quotients.

ex-gl2-quotient-by-diagonal-torus.title: The quotient of GL2 by the diagonal torus is the complement of the diagonal in P1 x P1
ex-gl2-quotient-by-diagonal-torus.statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $G=\mathrm{GL}_2$ with its standard representation on $V=k^2$ ([[lem-general-linear-group-scheme-and-its-coordinate-ring]]), and let $T\subseteq G$ be the diagonal torus, the closed subgroup scheme whose $R$-points are the invertible diagonal matrices ([[def-morphism-and-closed-subgroup-scheme]], [[lem-closed-subgroup-scheme-valued-point-criterion]]). (a) $T$ is a closed subgroup scheme of the smooth affine group scheme $G$, and the fppf quotient sheaf $G/T$ ([[def-quotient-sheaf-and-representable-quotient]]) is representable ([[thm-homogeneous-space-for-smooth-affine-group]]). (b) Let $G$ act on $Y=\mathbb P^1_k\times_k\mathbb P^1_k$ by the product of the actions induced on each factor by the standard representation ([[lem-projective-space-action-from-linear-representation]]), and let $o=(\langle e_1\rangle,\langle e_2\rangle)\in Y(k)$. Then the stabilizer of $o$ is $T$, the orbit $O_o$ is exactly the open subscheme $\{(L_1,L_2)\in Y: L_1\ne L_2\}$ (complement of the diagonal), and the orbit map induces an isomorphism $G/T\cong O_o$ ([[prop-faithfully-flat-orbit-map-represents-coset-quotient]], [[lem-orbit-map-fibres-and-stabilizer-dimension]]). (c) Consequently $G/T$ is a smooth separated finite-type $k$-scheme whose base change to an algebraic closure has dimension $2$ (equal to $\dim G-\dim T=4-2$, by the orbit-stabilizer dimension identity); the morphism $G/T\to\mathbb P^1_k$, $(L_1,L_2)\mapsto L_1$, has fibres isomorphic to $\mathbb P^1_k$ minus one point; and for every extension field $K/k$ the natural map $G(K)/T(K)\to(G/T)(K)$ is a bijection.
ex-gl2-quotient-by-diagonal-torus.strategy: Milne, Example 7.19 and Theorem 7.18, printed p. 143, computes the quotient of $\mathrm{GL}_2$ by a line stabilizer; here the subgroup is the diagonal torus rather than the Borel, and the orbit is taken on $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$. (a) The diagonal matrices form a closed subgroup scheme: they are cut out by the vanishing of the two off-diagonal coordinates, and the valued-point criterion identifies the closed subscheme they define with the functor $R\mapsto\{(R^\times)^2\}$; smoothness and affineness of $G$ are those of the published $\mathrm{GL}_2$ item. (b) The standard representation is faithful, so the induced action on $\mathbb P^1_k$ is the usual action on lines in $k^2$; the action on the product is the diagonal action. A matrix stabilizes the ordered pair $(\langle e_1\rangle,\langle e_2\rangle)$ exactly when it preserves both coordinate lines, i.e. is diagonal with unit entries. Transitivity on pairs of distinct lines: given distinct lines $L_1,L_2$ over any field $K$, choose nonzero $u\in L_1$, $v\in L_2$; they form a basis, and the matrix with columns $u,v$ lies in $G(K)$ and moves the standard pair to $(L_1,L_2)$. Hence $O_o$ is the complement of the diagonal; that complement is open because $Y$ is separated and the diagonal is a closed immersion. Since $G$ is smooth, the orbit map onto $O_o$ is faithfully flat of finite type, and the coset-quotient proposition identifies $G/T$ with $O_o$. (c) Smoothness and separatedness of $G/T$ follow from the locally closed smooth orbit and the open immersion into the separated scheme $Y$. For the dimension: after base change to an algebraic closure $\bar k$, the orbit-stabilizer dimension identity gives $\dim_{\bar k}(G/T)_{\bar k}=\dim G_{\bar k}-\dim T_{\bar k}=4-2=2$, using $\dim\mathrm{GL}_2=4$ (open in the fourfold affine space) and $\dim T=2$ ($T\cong\mathbf G_m^2$); dimension of a finite-type $k$-scheme is unchanged by passing to an algebraic closure. The fibres of the first projection over $L_1$ are the complement of the point $L_1$ in $\mathbb P^1$, and $K$-rational points of $O_o$ are the pairs of distinct $K$-rational lines, in bijection with $G(K)/T(K)$ by transitivity and the stabilizer computation.

cex-orbit-set-need-not-represent-quotien.title: The orbit set of k-points need not be the k-points of the fppf quotient sheaf
cex-orbit-set-need-not-represent-quotien.statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $\ne2$ containing a nonsquare $a\in k^\times$ (for example $k=\mathbb R$, $a=-1$). Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}k[x]/(x^2-a)$ and let $G=\mu_2=\operatorname{Spec}k[t]/(t^2-1)$ act on $X$ by the coaction $x\mapsto t\otimes x$, that is $g\cdot x=gx$ for $g\in\mu_2(R)$ ([[def-algebraic-group-action-and-scheme-theoretic-stabilizer]]). Then: (a) $X$ is finite étale of degree $2$ over $k$ ([[lem-finite-etale-algebra-module-presentation-and-rank]]) and $X(k)=\emptyset$, so the orbit set is empty; (b) the morphism $G\times_kX\to X\times_kX$, $(g,z)\mapsto(g\cdot z,z)$, is an isomorphism: on coordinate rings it is the $k$-algebra isomorphism $k[x,y]/(x^2-a,y^2-a)\to k[t,x]/(t^2-1,x^2-a)$, $x\mapsto tx$, $y\mapsto x$; hence the finite locally free equivalence relation $R=G\times_kX\rightrightarrows X$ has quotient $\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $X/G$ is represented by $\operatorname{Spec}k$ ([[thm-fppf-quotient-for-affine-finite-locally-free-equivalence-relation]]), so $(X/G)(k)=\{\ast\}$; (c) consequently the naive quotient presheaf $T\mapsto X(T)/G(T)$ is not the quotient sheaf $X/G$ ([[def-quotient-sheaf-and-representable-quotient]]): the class of the identity section $x\in X(X)$ is fixed by the two pullbacks along $X\times_kX\rightrightarrows X$ — the two pullbacks are the first and second projections and differ by multiplication by the unit $y/x\in\mu_2(X\times_kX)$ — but it is not the pullback of any class in $X(k)/G(k)=\emptyset$. Hence the orbit set does not represent the quotient sheaf: sheafification is strictly necessary, and $(X/G)(k)$ is not $X(k)/G(k)$.
cex-orbit-set-need-not-represent-quotien.strategy: Standard Galois-descent computation, structured as a counterexample to the statement that the naive quotient presheaf computes the fppf quotient. Setup: because $a$ is a nonsquare and $\operatorname{char}k\ne2$, $x^2-a$ is irreducible and separable, so $k[x]/(x^2-a)$ is a separable quadratic field extension $K/k$ and $X=\operatorname{Spec}K$ is finite étale of degree $2$ over $k$: the algebra is free of rank $2$ and finitely presented over $k$, and $\Omega_{A/k}=A\,dx/(2x\,dx)=0$ because $x$ (and hence $2x$) is a unit in $A$, so the published equivalence flat + unramified + finitely presented = étale applies. A $k$-algebra map $k[x]/(x^2-a)\to k$ would send $x$ to a square root of $a$, so $X(k)=\emptyset$. The cited isomorphism: in $k[x,y]/(x^2-a,y^2-a)$ one has $x^2=y^2=a\in k^\times$, so $x$ and $y$ are units; the displayed map is well defined and surjective because the images of $1,y,x,xy$ are $1,x,tx,txy$, which generate the target, while source and target are both free of rank $4$ over $k$, so the surjection is an isomorphism. Then $j=(t,s)$ is an isomorphism, $s=\mathrm{pr}_2$ and $t$ are finite locally free of rank $2$, and the published affine quotient theorem applies with invariants $C=\{f: s^\sharp(f)=t^\sharp(f)\}=k$ (a general element $\alpha+\beta x$ satisfies $t^\sharp(f)=s^\sharp(f)$ only when $\beta=0$, since $x$ is a unit and $t-1\ne0$ in $k[t,x]/(t^2-1,x^2-a)$); hence $X/G$ is represented by $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Failure of the sheaf property: over the fppf cover $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, the class of the identity section is a compatible family of sections of the presheaf that does not descend, since $X(k)/G(k)=\emptyset$; this exhibits the difference between the naive orbit set and the quotient sheaf. Note that the quotient sheaf here is representable: the counterexample separates the orbit set from the quotient sheaf, not representability from the quotient sheaf.
